card.occupation: Part-time sales and accounts administrator at a plumbing and heating supplies depot on an industrial estate in Rainham, about 25 hours a week over four days. He handles purchase orders, chases unpaid invoices from trade accounts and answers the phones when the counter is busy.
card.education_detail: Went to a local comprehensive in Gillingham and left with six GCSEs, mostly Cs, plus a D in maths that he resat and passed. Started a BTEC in Construction at MidKent College but dropped out in the second year when a mate's dad offered him labouring work. Has no qualifications since, apart from a forklift ticket that has lapsed.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom flat above a row of shops off the High Street with his girlfriend of seven years, Jade, who is a dental nurse. They have no children. They have talked about getting engaged, but neither of them has done anything about it. They have a ginger cat called Biscuit, which was Jade's idea.
card.cultural_background: White British and Kent born and bred. His family has been in the Medway towns for generations, and his grandad worked at Chatham Dockyard before it closed. He was christened Church of England and went to a C of E primary. He would tick 'Christian' on a form but only goes to church for weddings, funerals and sometimes the Christmas Eve service with his mum. He has a vague sense that he believes in something but doesn't think about it much.
card.professional_persona: Competent at the bits of the job he's done a hundred times and quick on the phone with tradesmen, because he speaks their language. He is disorganised with everything else. His desk is a mess of delivery notes and his email inbox has thousands unread. He forgets to log calls and leaves the end-of-month reconciliation until his manager, Karen, nags him. He went part-time after the depot cut hours two years ago and found he preferred it. He doesn't pretend to love the job and will say so if asked.
card.sports_persona: A Gillingham FC fan by default and a Chelsea fan on telly, because his dad was. He goes to Priestfield a few times a season with his brother and moans about the football the whole way home. He used to play five-a-side on Wednesdays but packed it in after rowing with a lad on the other team. He's naturally fit and has never been to a gym. He walks a lot because he doesn't like paying for parking.
card.arts_persona: Not really interested. He watches whatever is on Netflix that Jade picks, likes a crime drama or a gangster film, and has seen most of the Fast & Furious films more than once. He listens to the radio in the van-style hatchback he drives, mostly Heart or Kiss, and some old garage tunes from when he was a teenager. He hasn't been to a theatre since a school trip and wouldn't choose to.
card.travel_persona: Prefers the same places. They have done Tenerife three times and Benidorm once for a stag do. Jade wanted to try Portugal last year and he grumbled but went, and he admitted the food was alright. Weekend trips are Margate or Camber Sands. He hates flying delays and queues and is not adventurous about it.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. He calls the evening meal dinner, and it's usually something quick: pasta bake, chicken in the air fryer, oven chips. Jade does most of the cooking, and he does a fry-up on Sundays when he can be bothered. Friday is a Chinese takeaway from the same place every week, always salt and pepper chicken. He doesn't like anything too spicy or 'fancy'. He drinks Stella or Carling at the pub and has a can or two at home most evenings.
hobbies_and_interests: Playing FIFA/EA FC online with his brother and a couple of mates on headsets
Going to Gillingham home games now and then
Fantasy Premier League, though he often forgets to change his team
Pub quiz at the local on Thursdays, mostly for the pint
Watching boxing and UFC on pay-per-view with mates
Scrolling TikTok and football clips on his phone
skills: Quick and confident on the phone with trade customers
Knows plumbing and heating parts and codes well from years at the depot
Basic Sage and Excel, enough to get by
Can do odd jobs round the flat: putting up shelves, bleeding radiators
Good at FIFA, by his own account
Holds his ground in an argument
card.career_goals: No real plan. He would take more hours or a counter job if the money was better, and has half-thought about doing an electrician or gas course 'one day', but has never looked into it properly. Mainly he wants enough money to put down a deposit on a house with Jade before they're 40, and he knows that probably means he needs to sort himself out.
card.voice: Estuary-ish Kent accent, fairly relaxed pace, a bit flat and matter-of-fact. He drops t's ('wa'er', 'bo'ul') and says 'mate' a lot, plus 'yeah' and 'you know' as tags. He hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm', and uses 'sort of' when he's not sure. Now and then he slips into 'you was' or 'we was'. He uses 'knackered', 'skint' and 'proper' naturally. Answers tend to be short and to the point, and he can sound a bit blunt or impatient if a question seems pointless ('what, like, generally?'). When there's a silence he doesn't rush to fill it. He'll say 'yeah, that's it really' and wait for the next question.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital only if autocorrect does it. Few full stops and no apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Short answers, sometimes just a word or two. Uses 'tbh', 'idk', 'n/a' and the odd 'lol'. Typos are left in, and he never goes back to edit. If a question looks long he might type 'not sure really' and move on.
card.with_strangers: Polite enough at first but not especially warm. He's a bit guarded and slightly sceptical about why he's being asked things. He'll answer honestly, sometimes more bluntly than expected, and doesn't bother saying what he thinks you want to hear. He loosens up if the talk turns to football or work moans. He gets visibly bored if things drag or feel too abstract.
small_things: The depot coffee machine has been broken for three weeks and nobody's fixed it
The cat keeps sitting on his controller
Parking round the High Street is a nightmare
Gillingham lost again at the weekend
He's knackered because the neighbours were up late
Jade's mum is coming over Sunday
deeper_things: Feels a bit embarrassed that he's 33, part-time and still renting, while his younger brother has a house and a kid
Knows he's 'all talk' about sorting out a trade course and gets defensive if anyone pushes
His dad had a heart attack at 58, and it's made him think about the drinking a bit
He and Jade bicker about money and the marriage question more than he lets on
Still has a falling-out with an old best mate that he's too stubborn to fix
Doesn't really know what he thinks about God, but prayed when his dad was in hospital
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below face level, so the shot looks up at him a little. He's centred but a bit too close, cutting off at the shoulders. The lighting is warm and uneven, from a lamp off to the left and the grey-blue glow of a TV on the right, with the room otherwise fairly dim in the evening. He's a White man in his early thirties with a round-ish face, light stubble, short dark-brown hair in a skin fade with a bit more length on top, pushed forward. No glasses. His expression is neutral and slightly unimpressed, eyebrows a touch raised as if waiting for something to load. He's wearing a plain navy Nike hoodie. Behind him is a grey fabric corner settee with a crumpled fleece throw and a ginger cat asleep on one cushion. On the magnolia wall above is a cheap canvas print of the Thames at night. Part of a black PlayStation controller and a can of Carling sit on the arm of the settee. A doorway to a narrow hallway is visible at the top right, with a coat hanging on the door.
